15|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16|# 1. Unified Diff Pruner (diff_engine)
17|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
18|_DIFF_GIT_RE = re.compile(r"^diff --git a/.* b/.*")
19|_HUNK_HDR_RE = re.compile(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+\d+(?:,\d+)? @@.*", re.M)
20|_FILE_HDR_PREFIXES = ("--- ", "+++ ", "index ", "new file mode", "deleted file mode", "similarity index", "rename from", "rename to")
21|
22|_MIN_UNCHANGED_RUN = 6
23|_KEEP_CONTEXT = 2
24|
25|
26|def prune_unified_diff(text: str, budget: int = 200) -> str:
27|    """Compress unified diff text semantically without breaking hunk structures."""
28|    try:
29|        if not text or ("diff --git" not in text and not _HUNK_HDR_RE.search(text)):
30|            return text
31|
32|        lines = text.split("\n")
33|        out: list[str] = []
34|        unchanged_buf: list[str] = []
35|
36|        def _flush_unchanged() -> None:
37|            nonlocal unchanged_buf
38|            if not unchanged_buf:
39|                return
40|            n = len(unchanged_buf)
41|            if n <= _MIN_UNCHANGED_RUN:
42|                out.extend(unchanged_buf)
43|            else:
44|                out.extend(unchanged_buf[:_KEEP_CONTEXT])
45|                omitted = n - (_KEEP_CONTEXT * 2)
46|                out.append(f"  [... {omitted} unchanged lines ...]")
47|                out.extend(unchanged_buf[-_KEEP_CONTEXT:])
48|            unchanged_buf = []
49|
50|        for line in lines:
51|            if _DIFF_GIT_RE.match(line) or any(line.startswith(p) for p in _FILE_HDR_PREFIXES):
52|                _flush_unchanged()
53|                out.append(line)
54|            elif _HUNK_HDR_RE.match(line):
55|                _flush_unchanged()
56|                out.append(line)
57|            elif line.startswith("+") or line.startswith("-"):
58|                _flush_unchanged()
59|                out.append(line)
60|            elif line.startswith(" ") or line == "":
61|                unchanged_buf.append(line)
62|            else:
63|                _flush_unchanged()
64|                out.append(line)
65|
66|        _flush_unchanged()
67|        if budget > 0 and len(out) > budget:
68|            head_keep = max(1, budget - max(2, budget // 5))
69|            tail_keep = max(1, budget - head_keep)
70|            omitted_lines = len(out) - head_keep - tail_keep
71|            if omitted_lines > 0:
72|                out = (
73|                    out[:head_keep]
74|                    + [f"  [... {omitted_lines} diff lines omitted ...]"]
75|                    + out[-tail_keep:]
76|                )
77|        res = "\n".join(out)
78|        return res if len(res) < len(text) else text
79|    except Exception:
80|        return text

84|# 2. Traceback Pruner (traceback_pruner)
85|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
86|_PY_TB_START = re.compile(r"^\s*Traceback \(most recent call last\):")
87|_PY_FRAME_RE = re.compile(r"^  File \"([^\"]+)\", line (\d+), in (.*)$")
88|_JS_FRAME_RE = re.compile(r"^\s+at\s+(?:(?:new\s+)?([^\s(]+)\s+\()?(.*?)(?::(\d+):(\d+))?\)?$")
89|
90|_FRAMEWORK_PATH_RE = re.compile(
91|    r"(?i)(?:site-packages|dist-packages|node_modules|<frozen|lib[/\\]python\d|"
92|    r"unittest[/\\]case\.py|_pytest[/\\]|pluggy[/\\]|starlette[/\\]|"
93|    r"fastapi[/\\]|click[/\\]|tornado[/\\]|flask[/\\]|urllib3[/\\]|requests[/\\])"
94|)
95|
96|MIN_FRAMEWORK_RUN = 2
97|
98|
99|def _is_framework_path(path: str) -> bool:
100|    return bool(_FRAMEWORK_PATH_RE.search(path or ""))
101|

103|def prune_python_traceback(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
104|    """Parse and prune Python traceback blocks within a line list."""
105|    out: list[str] = []
106|    i = 0
107|    n = len(lines)
108|    while i < n:
109|        line = lines[i]
110|        if not _PY_TB_START.match(line):
111|            out.append(line)
112|            i += 1
113|            continue
114|
115|        tb_head = line
116|        i += 1
117|        frames: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
118|        while i < n:
119|            m = _PY_FRAME_RE.match(lines[i])
120|            if m:
121|                hdr = lines[i]
122|                code = ""
123|                i += 1
124|                if i < n and (lines[i].startswith("    ") or lines[i].startswith("\t")):
125|                    code = lines[i]
126|                    i += 1
127|                is_fw = _is_framework_path(m.group(1))
128|                frames.append((hdr, code, is_fw))
129|            else:
130|                break
131|
132|        if len(frames) <= 3:
133|            out.append(tb_head)
134|            for hdr, code, _ in frames:
135|                out.append(hdr)
136|                if code:
137|                    out.append(code)
138|            continue
139|
140|        kept_blocks: list[tuple[str, str] | str] = []
141|        kept_blocks.append((frames[0][0], frames[0][1]))
142|
143|        fw_run = 0
144|        j = 1
145|        m_frames = len(frames) - 1
146|        while j < m_frames:
147|            hdr, code, is_fw = frames[j]
148|            if is_fw:
149|                fw_run += 1
150|                j += 1
151|                continue
152|            if fw_run > 0:
153|                if fw_run >= MIN_FRAMEWORK_RUN:
154|                    kept_blocks.append(f"  [... {fw_run} framework frames omitted ...]")
155|                else:
156|                    for k in range(j - fw_run, j):
157|                        kept_blocks.append((frames[k][0], frames[k][1]))
158|                fw_run = 0
159|            kept_blocks.append((hdr, code))
160|            j += 1
161|
162|        if fw_run > 0:
163|            if fw_run >= MIN_FRAMEWORK_RUN:
164|                kept_blocks.append(f"  [... {fw_run} framework frames omitted ...]")
165|            else:
166|                for k in range(m_frames - fw_run, m_frames):
167|                    kept_blocks.append((frames[k][0], frames[k][1]))
168|
169|        kept_blocks.append((frames[-1][0], frames[-1][1]))
170|
171|        out.append(tb_head)
172|        for item in kept_blocks:
173|            if isinstance(item, str):
174|                out.append(item)
175|            else:
176|                out.append(item[0])
177|                if item[1]:
178|                    out.append(item[1])
179|
180|    return out

183|def prune_js_traceback(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
184|    """Parse and prune Node/JS traceback lines."""
185|    out: list[str] = []
186|    i = 0
187|    n = len(lines)
188|    while i < n:
189|        line = lines[i]
190|        if not _JS_FRAME_RE.match(line):
191|            out.append(line)
192|            i += 1
193|            continue
194|
195|        frames: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
196|        while i < n and _JS_FRAME_RE.match(lines[i]):
197|            hdr = lines[i]
198|            is_fw = _is_framework_path(hdr)
199|            frames.append((hdr, is_fw))
200|            i += 1
201|
202|        if len(frames) <= 3:
203|            for hdr, _ in frames:
204|                out.append(hdr)
205|            continue
206|
207|        out.append(frames[0][0])
208|        fw_run = 0
209|        j = 1
210|        m_frames = len(frames) - 1
211|        while j < m_frames:
212|            hdr, is_fw = frames[j]
213|            if is_fw:
214|                fw_run += 1
215|                j += 1
216|                continue
217|            if fw_run > 0:
218|                if fw_run >= MIN_FRAMEWORK_RUN:
219|                    out.append(f"    [... {fw_run} framework frames omitted ...]")
220|                else:
221|                    for k in range(j - fw_run, j):
222|                        out.append(frames[k][0])
223|                fw_run = 0
224|            out.append(hdr)
225|            j += 1
226|        if fw_run > 0:
227|            if fw_run >= MIN_FRAMEWORK_RUN:
228|                out.append(f"    [... {fw_run} framework frames omitted ...]")
229|            else:
230|                for k in range(m_frames - fw_run, m_frames):
231|                    out.append(frames[k][0])
232|        out.append(frames[-1][0])
233|
234|    return out
235|

237|def prune_traceback(text: str) -> str:
238|    """Entry point: inspect text and prune recognized framework frames."""
239|    try:
240|        if not text:
241|            return text
242|        has_py = "Traceback (most recent call last):" in text
243|        has_js = "\n    at " in text or "\n  at " in text or text.startswith("    at ") or text.startswith("  at ")
244|        if not has_py and not has_js:
245|            return text
246|        lines = text.split("\n")
247|        if has_py:
248|            lines = prune_python_traceback(lines)
249|        if has_js:
250|            lines = prune_js_traceback(lines)
251|        res = "\n".join(lines)
252|        return res if len(res) < len(text) else text
253|    except Exception:
254|        return text

260|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
261|# 3. Scoped Search Grouping (scoped_search)
262|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
263|_HIT_RE = re.compile(r"^([\w./\\~$@+:-]+?):(\d+):(.*)$")
264|_DEF_RE = re.compile(
265|    r"^\s*(?:async\s+)?(?:def|class|func(?:tion)?|fn)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)"
266|)
267|
268|_MIN_LINES = 12
269|_MIN_HITS = 10
270|_MIN_PATHS = 2
271|_HIT_FRACTION = 0.6
272|_KEEP_ALL = 3
273|_MIN_RUN = 2
274|_MAX_DEFS = 2
275|
276|
277|def looks_search_shaped(text: str) -> bool:
278|    """True when the doc is a multi-file path:line:text hit list."""
279|    try:
280|        lines = [ln for ln in (text or "").split("\n") if ln.strip()]
281|        if len(lines) < _MIN_LINES:
282|            return False
283|        hits = 0
284|        paths: set[str] = set()
285|        for ln in lines:
286|            m = _HIT_RE.match(ln)
287|            if m:
288|                hits += 1
289|                paths.add(m.group(1))
290|        if hits < _MIN_HITS or len(paths) < _MIN_PATHS:
291|            return False
292|        return hits / len(lines) >= _HIT_FRACTION
293|    except Exception:
294|        return False
295|
296|
297|def _render_segment(
298|    path: str,
299|    hits: list[tuple[int, str, str]],
300|    owner: str | None,
301|    deadline: Any | None,
302|) -> list[str]:
303|    raw = [h[2] for h in hits]
304|    n = len(hits)
305|    if n <= _KEEP_ALL:
306|        return raw
307|    keep = {0, n - 1}
308|    for i, (_, _, line) in enumerate(hits):
309|        if is_important(line):
310|            keep.add(i)
311|    defs: list[str] = []
312|    seen: set[str] = set()
313|    total_defs = 0
314|    for lineno, text, _ in hits:
315|        m = _DEF_RE.match(text)
316|        if m:
317|            total_defs += 1
318|            name = m.group(1)
319|            if name not in seen and len(defs) < _MAX_DEFS:
320|                seen.add(name)
321|                defs.append(f"{name}@L{lineno}")
322|    header = f"=== {path} ({n} hits)"
323|    if defs:
324|        extra = total_defs - len(defs)
325|        header += " [defs: " + " ".join(defs) + (f" …+{extra}" if extra > 0 else "") + "]"
326|    header += " ==="
327|
328|    out: list[str] = []
329|    run: list[int] = []
330|    folded_any = False
331|
332|    def _flush() -> None:
333|        nonlocal folded_any
334|        if not run:
335|            return
336|        if len(run) >= _MIN_RUN:
337|            out.append(seen_lines(len(run), owner or ""))
338|            folded_any = True
339|        else:
340|            out.extend(raw[k] for k in run)
341|        run.clear()
342|
343|    for i in range(n):
344|        if deadline is not None and (i & 255) == 0:
345|            deadline.check()
346|        if i in keep:
347|            _flush()
348|            out.append(raw[i])
349|        else:
350|            run.append(i)
351|    _flush()
352|    if not folded_any:
353|        return raw
354|    return [header] + out
355|

357|def group_search_hits(
358|    text: str,
359|    owner: str | None = None,
360|    deadline: Any | None = None,
361|) -> tuple[str, int]:
362|    """Collapse multi-file search hits into file-grouped blocks."""
363|    try:
364|        if not looks_search_shaped(text):
365|            return text, 0
366|        lines = text.split("\n")
367|        out: list[str] = []
368|        seg_path: str | None = None
369|        seg_hits: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []
370|
371|        def _flush_seg() -> None:
372|            nonlocal seg_path, seg_hits
373|            if seg_path is not None:
374|                out.extend(_render_segment(seg_path, seg_hits, owner, deadline))
375|            seg_path = None
376|            seg_hits = []
377|
378|        for ln in lines:
379|            m = _HIT_RE.match(ln)
380|            if m:
381|                path = m.group(1)
382|                if seg_path is not None and path != seg_path:
383|                    _flush_seg()
384|                seg_path = path
385|                seg_hits.append((int(m.group(2)), m.group(3), ln))
386|            else:
387|                _flush_seg()
388|                out.append(ln)
389|        _flush_seg()
390|        new_text = "\n".join(out)
391|        saved = len(text) - len(new_text)
392|        if saved <= 0:
393|            return text, 0
394|        return new_text, saved
395|    except Exception:
396|        return text, 0

400|# 4. AST Code Skeletonizer (Language-Agnostic Structure Extractor)
401|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
402|_CODE_DEF_RE = re.compile(
403|    r"^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)(?P<decl>(?:async\s+)?(?:def|class|function|fn|pub\s+fn|func|interface|struct|type)\s+[A-Za-z0-9_$]+[^{:]*[:{])"
404|)
405|_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*(?:import|from|require|use|package|include)\b")
406|
407|
408|def skeletonize_code(code: str, max_body_lines: int = 5) -> str:
409|    """Extract signatures, docstrings, and imports while folding deep bodies."""
410|    if not code or len(code) < 2048:
411|        return code
412|    lines = code.split("\n")
413|    if len(lines) < 50:
414|        return code
415|
416|    out: list[str] = []
417|    i = 0
418|    n = len(lines)
419|    while i < n:
420|        line = lines[i]
421|        if _IMPORT_RE.match(line) or line.strip().startswith(("@", "#", "//", "/*")):
422|            out.append(line)
423|            i += 1
424|            continue
425|
426|        m = _CODE_DEF_RE.match(line)
427|        if m:
428|            out.append(line)
429|            indent = len(m.group("indent"))
430|            i += 1
431|            body_count = 0
432|            while i < n:
433|                cur = lines[i]
434|                cur_indent = len(cur) - len(cur.lstrip(" \t")) if cur.strip() else indent + 4
435|                if cur.strip() and cur_indent <= indent:
436|                    break
437|                if body_count < max_body_lines:
438|                    out.append(cur)
439|                    body_count += 1
440|                elif body_count == max_body_lines:
441|                    out.append(" " * (indent + 4) + "[... implementation body folded ...]")
442|                    body_count += 1
443|                i += 1
444|            continue
445|
446|        out.append(line)
447|        i += 1
448|
449|    res = "\n".join(out)
450|    return res if len(res) < len(code) else code

453|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
454|# 5. Line-Anchored Smart AST Skeletonizer (v4.2)
455|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
456|_MIN_FOLD_BODY_LINES = 15  # functions of 15 lines or fewer are never folded
457|
458|
459|def smart_skeletonize_code(
460|    text: str,
461|    ref: str = "",
462|    *,
463|    min_body_lines: int = _MIN_FOLD_BODY_LINES,
464|    line_prefixes: list[str] | None = None,
465|    line_nos: list[int] | None = None,
466|) -> tuple[str, int, int]:
467|    """Line-anchored AST code skeletonizer with Zero Loss of Signatures/Types.
468|
469|    When `line_prefixes` / `line_nos` are provided (Hermes `LINE|CONTENT`
470|    output), `text` must be the unprefixed source and the skeleton re-attaches
471|    the exact original `LINE|` prefix to every kept line.
472|
473|    Preserves 100% of:
474|      - Imports, module constants, global assignments, type definitions
475|      - Class/Function decorators, full multi-line signatures & type annotations
476|      - First line of docstrings
477|      - Short functions/methods (<= min_body_lines)
478|      - Final return/yield/raise statement of folded functions (for return-type clarity)
479|    Replaces only the interior implementation body of long functions with an exact
480|    1-indexed line-range marker so the agent can call read_file(offset=..., limit=...).
481|
482|    Returns: (skeleton_text, saved_chars, folded_functions_count)
483|    """
484|    try:
485|        tree = ast.parse(text)
486|    except Exception:
487|        return text, 0, 0
488|
489|    lines = text.split("\n")
490|    total_lines = len(lines)
491|    use_prefixes = (
492|        line_prefixes is not None
493|        and line_nos is not None
494|        and len(line_prefixes) == total_lines
495|        and len(line_nos) == total_lines
496|    )
497|    # Ranges to fold: (fold_start_1idx, fold_end_1idx, indent_str, func_name)
498|    fold_ranges: list[tuple[int, int, str, str]] = []
499|
500|    for node in ast.walk(tree):
501|        if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
502|            continue
503|        if not getattr(node, "body", None) or not hasattr(node, "end_lineno"):
504|            continue
505|        # Skip folding nested functions inside a parent that is itself folded.
506|        first_stmt = node.body[0]
507|        first_fold_stmt = first_stmt
508|        body_start = first_stmt.lineno  # 1-indexed
509|
510|        # If the first statement is a docstring, keep the docstring lines and start
511|        # folding right after it -- the range must stay contiguous or the retrieval
512|        # coordinates in the marker no longer match the file.
513|        if (
514|            isinstance(first_stmt, ast.Expr)
515|            and isinstance(getattr(first_stmt, "value", None), ast.Constant)
516|            and isinstance(first_stmt.value.value, str)
517|        ):
518|            if len(node.body) <= 1:
519|                continue  # docstring only -> nothing to fold
520|            doc_end = getattr(first_stmt, "end_lineno", first_stmt.lineno) or first_stmt.lineno
521|            first_fold_stmt = node.body[1]
522|            body_start = doc_end + 1
523|
524|        # A nested decorated def has its decorator on the line ABOVE stmt.lineno,
525|        # so folding from stmt.lineno would leave "@decorator" above the `pass`
526|        # -> SyntaxError. Start the fold at the decorator instead.
527|        decs = getattr(first_fold_stmt, "decorator_list", None)
528|        if decs:
529|            body_start = min(body_start, min(getattr(d, "lineno", first_fold_stmt.lineno) for d in decs))
530|
531|        body_end = node.end_lineno or body_start
532|
533|        # If the last statement is a short return/raise, keep it (return-type clarity).
534|        last_stmt = node.body[-1]
535|        if (
536|            last_stmt is not first_fold_stmt
537|            and isinstance(last_stmt, (ast.Return, ast.Raise))
538|            and hasattr(last_stmt, "lineno")
539|        ):
540|            last_span = (getattr(last_stmt, "end_lineno", last_stmt.lineno) or last_stmt.lineno) - last_stmt.lineno + 1
541|            if last_span <= 2 and last_stmt.lineno > body_start:
542|                body_end = last_stmt.lineno - 1
543|
544|        span_lines = body_end - body_start + 1
545|        if span_lines < min_body_lines:
546|            continue
547|
548|        # Indent from the first folded STATEMENT's own line. Reading it from the
549|        # line after a docstring hit the blank line -> indent 0 -> the `pass`
550|        # dedented out of the method -> IndentationError.
551|        stmt_line = lines[first_fold_stmt.lineno - 1] if 1 <= first_fold_stmt.lineno <= total_lines else ""
552|        indent_len = len(stmt_line) - len(stmt_line.lstrip(" \t"))
553|        if indent_len > 0:
554|            indent = stmt_line[:indent_len]
555|        else:
556|            indent = " " * (getattr(first_fold_stmt, "col_offset", None)
557|                            or getattr(node, "col_offset", 0) + 4)
558|        fold_ranges.append((body_start, body_end, indent, node.name))
559|
560|    if not fold_ranges:
561|        return text, 0, 0
562|
563|    # Sort and drop overlapping ranges (keep the outermost).
564|    fold_ranges.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], -(r[1] - r[0])))
565|    merged_ranges: list[tuple[int, int, str, str]] = []
566|    last_end = 0
567|    for s, e, ind, fn in fold_ranges:
568|        if s <= last_end:
569|            continue
570|        merged_ranges.append((s, e, ind, fn))
571|        last_end = e
572|
573|    ref_tag = f" {ref}" if ref else ""
574|    out: list[str] = []
575|    cur = 1  # 1-indexed line pointer
576|    for s, e, ind, fn in merged_ranges:
577|        while cur < s and cur <= total_lines:
578|            prefix = line_prefixes[cur - 1] if use_prefixes else ""  # type: ignore[index]
579|            out.append(f"{prefix}{lines[cur - 1]}")
580|            cur += 1
581|        # Markers and hints must carry the REAL file line numbers, not the
582|        # position inside the payload (Hermes `LINE|CONTENT` numbers are the
583|        # file's own line numbers).
584|        file_s = line_nos[s - 1] if use_prefixes else s  # type: ignore[index]
585|        file_e = line_nos[e - 1] if use_prefixes else e  # type: ignore[index]
586|        omitted = file_e - file_s + 1
587|        marker_prefix = line_prefixes[s - 1] if use_prefixes else ""  # type: ignore[index]
588|        # The marker must remain a valid Python statement: a bare comment line
589|        # would be an IndentationError when it is the only statement of a body.
590|        marker = (
591|            f"{marker_prefix}{ind}pass  # [tt:body L{file_s}-L{file_e} ({omitted}L of {fn}){ref_tag} "
592|            f"-> use read_file(offset={file_s}, limit={omitted}) or trimtok_retrieve]"
593|        )
